title: Auto-stop and rollback canary rollouts on SLO breach (5xx/timeouts/p95 latency)
creator: Sean Gallagher
description:
Implement automatic stop conditions for Hosted canary rollouts and wire them into the rollout orchestrator.

Scope:
- Evaluate SLO regressions comparing baseline vs canary cohorts:
  - 5xx error rate
  - timeout rate
  - p95 latency regression
- When stop condition trips, orchestrator should either:
  - auto-pause (default for Beta), or
  - auto-rollback (GA default for tenants with guardrail policy enabled), depending on tenant policy + rollout configuration.
- Notify: Console surface "Auto-stopped" reason + event timeline entry; send internal notification (PagerDuty for severe, Slack for non-severe) + optional customer email/webhook (if enabled for tenant).

Non-goals:
- Automated quality gates as a hard blocker (still allow optional manual quality metrics display; no automated gating in this ticket).

Notes:
- Must be safe under partial telemetry outages: avoid silent failures; avoid rollouts getting stuck indefinitely; ensure deterministic behavior on metric fetch timeouts.
- Must be tunable by tier/region without creating metric-cardinality blowups.

Related artifacts:
- PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-28845-auto-stop-rollback-on-slo-breach.json
- Bugfix: sources/github/redwood/pr-28895-fix-rollout-step-stuck-on-metric-timeout.json
- SRE signals doc: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/hosted-rollouts-slo-metrics-and-alerts.json
acceptance_criteria:
1) During a running canary step, if canary 5xx rate exceeds threshold (absolute OR relative over baseline per policy), orchestrator transitions to AUTO_PAUSED or AUTO_ROLLED_BACK and emits events.
2) During a running canary step, if canary timeout rate exceeds threshold, orchestrator transitions to AUTO_PAUSED or AUTO_ROLLED_BACK and emits events.
3) During a running canary step, if canary p95 latency regression exceeds threshold (relative to baseline, with minimum sample requirements), orchestrator transitions to AUTO_PAUSED or AUTO_ROLLED_BACK and emits events.
4) Auto-stop decision is recorded in rollout activity timeline and audit logs include actor = system + reason payload.
5) Console can show clear reason + metrics snapshot used for decision (time window, cohorts, values) with a link to dashboards.
6) If telemetry query times out or returns insufficient samples, rollout does not hang; system either retries with backoff or marks evaluation as INCONCLUSIVE and continues to soak (policy-driven) while surfacing a warning.
7) End-to-end: canary split is set back to 0% (rollback) or held (pause) within 60s of stop condition trigger in at least 2 regions in staging.
implementation_notes:
High-level design:
- Evaluator runs on orchestrator side on a cadence (default 60s) while rollout is in RUNNING state and step is ACTIVE.
- Evaluator queries cohort metrics aggregated by telemetry service using tags: route_id, rollout_id, cohort=baseline|canary, region (bounded set), and status_class.
- Enforce minimum sample sizes to reduce flakiness:
  - min_requests_total (baseline+canary) and min_canary_requests
  - min_soak_seconds before first evaluation (e.g., 300s) unless explicitly overridden by policy
- Stop condition definitions:
  - 5xx: canary_5xx_rate > max(absolute_threshold, baseline_5xx_rate * (1 + relative_multiplier))
  - timeouts: canary_timeout_rate > max(absolute_threshold, baseline_timeout_rate * (1 + relative_multiplier))
  - p95 latency: canary_p95_ms > baseline_p95_ms * (1 + relative_multiplier) AND baseline_p95_ms > min_baseline_ms (avoid noisy tiny baselines)
- Decision outputs:
  - PASS (no action)
  - WARN (insufficient samples / transient telemetry issues; surface banner in Console)
  - FAIL (trip stop condition; action = PAUSE or ROLLBACK)

State machine wiring:
- New internal transition reason codes:
  - AUTO_STOP_5XX
  - AUTO_STOP_TIMEOUT
  - AUTO_STOP_P95_LATENCY
  - AUTO_STOP_METRICS_UNAVAILABLE (warn-only; does not change state by default)
- Actions:
  - AUTO_PAUSE: freeze at current split, stop auto-advancing, require human action to continue/rollback
  - AUTO_ROLLBACK: set split to 0% canary immediately, mark step as FAILED, mark rollout state as ROLLED_BACK

Policy/config:
- Respect policy engine guardrails (ENG-9146):
  - whether auto-rollback is allowed for tenant
  - required approvals before continuing after auto-pause
  - max evaluation frequency (avoid thundering herd)
- Defaults chosen with SRE (see comments):
  - evaluation_interval_seconds=60
  - first_eval_after_seconds=300
  - min_canary_requests=200 (scaled down automatically for low-traffic routes only if tenant explicitly opts-in)

Failure modes handled:
- Telemetry query timeout: retry 3x with jittered backoff; if still failing, emit WARN event + surface in Console; do not deadlock the step.
- Orchestrator restart: evaluator resumes using persisted last_evaluated_at; avoid duplicative stop events by using idempotency key (rollout_id+step_id+reason+window_end).
- Region skew: evaluator checks both global aggregate and per-region; FAIL if global fails OR any region exceeds hard threshold, but only if region has min samples.

Notifications:
- Internal: send Slack message to #eng-sre (non-page) on AUTO_PAUSE; trigger PagerDuty only if stop reason is 5xx/timeout above paging thresholds AND tenant tier is Enterprise.
- Customer-facing: add timeline entry visible in Console with "Auto-paused due to latency regression" and include window + suggested next steps; optional webhook event rollout.auto_paused / rollout.auto_rolled_back.
testing:
Unit tests:
- Stop condition math + sample-size gating
- Idempotency behavior for duplicate evaluator ticks
- State transitions for AUTO_PAUSE vs AUTO_ROLLBACK

Integration tests (staging):
- Synthetic load generator: inject 5xx/timeout/latency on canary backend; verify auto action within 60-120s
- Telemetry outage simulation: metrics service returns timeout; verify WARN event and rollout remains RUNNING (no stuck step)

E2E coverage:
- Included in ENG-9164 / PR-28933: create rollout -> start -> trip latency -> auto-pause -> manual rollback

Operational validation:
- Dashboards: verify cohort panels populate with rollout_id/cohort tags without cardinality spikes (see cardinality analysis doc).
rollout_plan:
1) Ship behind feature flag rollout_auto_stop_v1 (default off).
2) Enable in staging + dogfood tenants; run perf-canary smoke tests (perf-canary/pr-147).
3) Enable for 2-3 beta design partners with SRE monitoring and tuned thresholds.
4) For GA: default action = AUTO_ROLLBACK for tenants with policy guardrails enabled; keep AUTO_PAUSE for legacy tenants until they opt in.
5) Document in internal runbook + add on-call alert routing.
comments: 2025-02-11 (Hannah Rivera): Kicking off. Plan is to keep evaluator logic in orchestrator (not data plane) so we can reason about state transitions + audit events centrally. Need to align thresholds + sample size requirements with Sean/Aisha; initial proposal in implementation notes.

2025-02-12 (Aisha Bello): Please ensure we don’t page on every auto-pause. Suggest: PD only when (a) error/timeout hard threshold is exceeded and (b) tenant tier requires SLO paging. Everything else -> Slack + Console banner. Also add a "metrics unavailable" warning state; we’ve seen transient gaps in cohort tags during deploys.

2025-02-14 (Logan Wright): Telemetry tagging for rollout_id/cohort will be ready behind rollout_cohort_tags_v1 in ENG-9152. For evaluator queries, prefer using the rollup endpoint (1m buckets) vs raw traces. Cardinality: do NOT add model_version to these queries; route_id + rollout_id + cohort + region is already tight. We can provide aggregate by route+rollout for UI and evaluator.

2025-02-18 (Sean Gallagher): Default thresholds for beta: 5xx absolute 1% OR 3x baseline; timeouts absolute 0.5% OR 2x baseline; p95 regression 25% over baseline. Require 5 min soak before first evaluation and min 200 canary requests. Make these policy-configurable per tenant. Also need explicit behavior on telemetry query timeout (no stuck rollouts).

2025-02-25 (Hannah Rivera): PR up with core wiring + stop conditions: pr-28845. Remaining: idempotency + better handling of metrics timeouts; currently can stall if metrics endpoint is slow and evaluator tick overlaps.

2025-03-04 (Rafael Mendes): We hit a beta incident where the step got stuck due to metrics timeout and the UI just showed "Evaluating" indefinitely. Please ensure orchestrator transitions to WARN and continues soaking (or at least makes it actionable) instead of deadlocking. Tie to runbook steps (how to force pause/rollback).

2025-03-06 (Hannah Rivera): Shipped bugfix for stuck-on-timeout behavior: pr-28895. Added bounded retries + jitter and emit WARN timeline event when metrics are unavailable > 5m. Rollout continues soaking and re-evaluates next tick.

2025-03-12 (Jordan Lee): Confirming policy integration: auto-rollback is only allowed when tenant policy enables it + caller has permission to configure auto actions. System-triggered rollback should be allowed regardless of human approver role, but must be audited with actor=system and reason code. This aligns with audit requirements from Marcus.

2025-03-18 (Marcus Lin): Please ensure audit event includes the exact stop-condition fields used (thresholds, baseline/canary observed values, time window). Doesn’t need to be queryable fields, but must be included in the event payload for investigations and customer evidence requests.

2025-03-21 (Hannah Rivera): Marking done. Merged pr-28845 + pr-28895. Verified in staging with injected latency + 5xx faults; auto-rollback resets split within ~45s. WARN path works when telemetry endpoint times out; no more stuck steps. Next: verify e2e tests in ENG-9164 remain stable and update runbook references.
